gloss: To seek fish by climbing a tree; pursuing the impossible.
teaser: Ever tried to catch a fish by climbing a tree? Let's dive into this idiom!
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever tried to catch a fish by climbing a tree? Let's dive into this idiom! [break 1s] The phrase is: 缘木求鱼, yuán mù qiú yú. [break 1s] 缘 (yuán) - to be related or connected; [break 0.5s] 木 (mù) - tree; [break 0.5s] 求 (qiú) - to seek or ask for; [break 0.5s] 鱼 (yú) - fish. [break 1s] The full idiom is 缘木求鱼, which literally means 'to seek fish by climbing a tree' and figuratively signifies pursuing something impossible. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a story in ancient China where someone tried to catch fish by climbing a tree, which is obviously futile. It highlights the absurdity of trying to achieve something that cannot be done, emphasizing that the approach must match the goal. This phrase serves as a reminder to use the right methods to achieve our objectives. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他想通过赌博致富，真是缘木求鱼。 [break 1s] He thinks he can get rich by gambling; that's truly seeking fish by climbing a tree. [break 1s] Example 2: 如果你不学习，却想考试得高分，那就是缘木求鱼。 [break 1s] If you don’t study but want to score high on the exam, that’s just seeking fish by climbing a tree. [break 1s] Example 3: 他们试图通过不合法的手段获得成功，完全是缘木求鱼。 [break 1s] They are trying to achieve success through illegal means, which is completely seeking fish by climbing a tree. [break 1s] So, remember, 缘木求鱼 means to pursue the impossible. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
